Matter and Measurement: Matter
Anything that has mass and occupies space
Element
A pure substance that cannot be broken down chemically
Compound
A substance of two or more elements chemically bonded in fixed ratio
Mixture
A physical combination of substances that keep their own properties
Homogeneous mixture
A mixture with uniform composition throughout, such as a solution
Heterogeneous mixture
A mixture with visibly different regions or phases
Physical property
A characteristic observable without changing the substance's identity
Chemical property
A characteristic describing how a substance reacts to form new substances
Significant figures
The digits in a measurement that carry meaningful precision
Accuracy
How close a measurement is to the true accepted value
Precision
How closely repeated measurements agree with each other
Density
Mass divided by volume, an intensive property of a substance
Atomic Structure and Theory: Proton
Positively charged subatomic particle in the nucleus
Neutron
Neutral subatomic particle in the nucleus
Electron
Negatively charged subatomic particle orbiting the nucleus
Atomic number
The number of protons, which defines the element
Mass number
The total count of protons plus neutrons in a nucleus
Isotope
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Ion
An atom that has gained or lost electrons and carries a charge
Cation
A positively charged ion formed by losing electrons
Anion
A negatively charged ion formed by gaining electrons
Atomic mass unit
One twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom
Rutherford's gold foil experiment
Experiment showing the atom has a small dense positive nucleus
Dalton's atomic theory
Proposal that elements are made of identical indivisible atoms
Electron Configuration: Orbital
A region of space where an electron is most likely found
Valence electrons
Electrons in the outermost shell that determine bonding
Aufbau principle
Electrons fill the lowest energy orbitals first
Pauli exclusion principle
No two electrons in an atom share all four quantum numbers
Hund's rule
Electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly before pairing
Ground state
The lowest energy arrangement of an atom's electrons
Excited state
A higher energy arrangement after an electron absorbs energy
Electron cloud model
Model describing electron position as probability rather than fixed orbit
Noble gas configuration
Shorthand notation using the previous noble gas core
Octet rule
Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to reach eight valence electrons
The Periodic Table and Trends: A horizontal row of the periodic table
A vertical column whose elements share valence electron count
Group 1 elements, highly reactive with one valence electron
Group 2 elements with two valence electrons
Group 18 elements with full valence shells and very low reactivity
Groups 3 through 12, often forming colored compounds
Half the distance between nuclei of two bonded identical atoms
Energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom
An atom's tendency to attract shared electrons in a bond
An element with properties between metals and nonmetals
Element properties repeat periodically when ordered by atomic number
Ionic and Metallic Bonding: Ionic bond
Bond formed by the transfer of electrons between metal and nonmetal
Metallic bond
Attraction between metal cations and a sea of delocalized electrons
Crystal lattice
The repeating three-dimensional arrangement of ions in a solid
Electrolyte
A substance that conducts electricity when dissolved or molten
Malleability
The ability to be hammered into sheets, characteristic of metals
Ductility
The ability to be drawn into wire
Formula unit
The lowest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound
Alloy
A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements
Lattice energy
Energy released when gaseous ions form one mole of an ionic solid
Delocalized electrons
Electrons free to move throughout a metal structure
Covalent Bonding and Molecular Geometry: Covalent bond
Bond formed by sharing electron pairs between nonmetals
Single bond
A covalent bond sharing one pair of electrons
Double bond
A covalent bond sharing two pairs of electrons
Triple bond
A covalent bond sharing three pairs of electrons
Polar covalent bond
A bond with unequal electron sharing due to electronegativity difference
Nonpolar covalent bond
A bond with essentially equal electron sharing
Lewis structure
A diagram showing valence electrons and bonds in a molecule
VSEPR theory
Model predicting molecular shape from valence electron pair repulsion
Lone pair
A valence electron pair not involved in bonding
Tetrahedral
Molecular geometry with four bonding regions at about 109.5 degrees
Trigonal planar
Flat geometry with three bonding regions at 120 degrees
Bent geometry
Shape resulting from lone pairs compressing the bond angle, as in water
Chemical Nomenclature: Binary ionic compound
A compound of one metal and one nonmetal
Polyatomic ion
A charged group of covalently bonded atoms, such as sulfate
Roman numeral in a name
Indicates the charge of a transition metal cation
Prefix system
Naming method for covalent compounds using mono, di, tri, and so on
Sulfate
The polyatomic ion SO4 with a 2 minus charge
Nitrate
The polyatomic ion NO3 with a 1 minus charge
Carbonate
The polyatomic ion CO3 with a 2 minus charge
Ammonium
The polyatomic ion NH4 with a 1 plus charge
Hydroxide
The polyatomic ion OH with a 1 minus charge
Phosphate
The polyatomic ion PO4 with a 3 minus charge
Chemical Reactions and Equations: Synthesis reaction
Two or more reactants combine into a single product
Decomposition reaction
A single compound breaks down into simpler substances
Single replacement
One element replaces another in a compound
Double replacement
Two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds
Combustion reaction
A substance reacts rapidly with oxygen releasing heat and light
Law of conservation of mass
Mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
Coefficient
The number placed before a formula to balance an equation
Subscript
The number indicating how many atoms of an element are in a formula
Precipitate
An insoluble solid formed during a reaction in solution
Catalyst
A substance that speeds a reaction without being consumed
Endothermic reaction
A reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings
Exothermic reaction
A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings
Stoichiometry: Mole
The amount of substance containing 6.022 times 10 to the 23rd particles
Avogadro's number
6.022 times 10 to the 23rd, the number of particles in a mole
Molar mass
The mass in grams of one mole of a substance
Mole ratio
The ratio of coefficients between substances in a balanced equation
Limiting reactant
The reactant that runs out first and caps the product formed
Excess reactant
The reactant remaining after the limiting reactant is consumed
Theoretical yield
The maximum product predicted by stoichiometric calculation
Actual yield
The amount of product actually obtained in an experiment
Percent yield
Actual yield divided by theoretical yield, times 100
Empirical formula
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound
Molecular formula
The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule
Percent composition
The percentage by mass of each element in a compound
States of Matter and Gas Laws: Kinetic molecular theory
Model describing gases as small particles in constant random motion
Boyle's law
At constant temperature, pressure and volume are inversely proportional
Charles's law
At constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to Kelvin temperature
Gay-Lussac's law
At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to temperature
Combined gas law
Relationship combining pressure, volume, and temperature
Ideal gas law
PV equals nRT, relating pressure, volume, moles, and temperature
STP
Standard temperature and pressure: 0 degrees Celsius and 1 atmosphere
Dalton's law of partial pressures
Total pressure equals the sum of individual gas pressures
Sublimation
A solid changing directly into a gas
Deposition
A gas changing directly into a solid
Vapor pressure
The pressure exerted by a vapor in equilibrium with its liquid
Phase diagram
A graph showing the states of a substance across pressure and temperature
Solutions and Solubility: Solute
The substance being dissolved in a solution
Solvent
The substance doing the dissolving, present in greater amount
Molarity
Moles of solute per liter of solution
Saturated solution
A solution holding the maximum dissolvable solute at that temperature
Unsaturated solution
A solution that can still dissolve more solute
Supersaturated solution
An unstable solution holding more solute than normally possible
Solubility
The maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given solvent
Dilution
Adding solvent to lower the concentration of a solution
Miscible
Describing liquids that dissolve in each other in any proportion
Colligative property
A property depending on solute particle count, not identity
Acids, Bases, and pH: A substance that donates protons and produces hydrogen ions in water
A substance that accepts protons or produces hydroxide ions in water
A logarithmic scale measuring hydrogen ion concentration from 0 to 14
Reaction of an acid and base producing salt and water
A substance that increases hydrogen ion concentration in water
An acid that ionizes completely in water
An acid that only partially ionizes in water
Procedure determining concentration by adding a known solution to an endpoint
A substance that changes color at a particular pH
A solution resisting pH change when small amounts of acid or base are added
The point in a titration where moles of acid equal moles of base
Thermochemistry: Enthalpy
The heat content of a system at constant pressure, symbol H
Specific heat capacity
Energy needed to raise one gram of a substance by one degree Celsius
Calorimetry
Measuring heat transfer during a physical or chemical change
Exothermic process
A process releasing heat, with negative enthalpy change
Endothermic process
A process absorbing heat, with positive enthalpy change
Heat of fusion
Energy required to melt one gram of a solid
Heat of vaporization
Energy required to vaporize one gram of a liquid
Hess's law
Total enthalpy change is the same regardless of reaction pathway
System
The specific part of the universe being studied
Surroundings
Everything outside the system that can exchange energy with it
Reaction Rates and Equilibrium: Reaction rate
How quickly reactants are converted into products
Activation energy
The minimum energy required for a reaction to occur
Collision theory
Reactions occur when particles collide with enough energy and correct orientation
Chemical equilibrium
State where forward and reverse reaction rates are equal
Le Chatelier's principle
A system at equilibrium shifts to relieve an applied stress
Equilibrium constant
Ratio of product to reactant concentrations at equilibrium
Reversible reaction
A reaction that can proceed in both directions
Dynamic equilibrium
Ongoing forward and reverse reactions with no net concentration change
Inhibitor
A substance that slows a reaction rate
Reaction mechanism
The step-by-step sequence by which a reaction occurs
Nuclear Chemistry: Radioactivity
Spontaneous emission of particles or energy from an unstable nucleus
Alpha particle
A helium nucleus emitted in radioactive decay, weakly penetrating
Beta particle
A high-speed electron emitted when a neutron converts to a proton
Gamma ray
High-energy electromagnetic radiation with strong penetrating power
Half-life
The time required for half a radioactive sample to decay
Nuclear fission
Splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei, releasing energy
Nuclear fusion
Combining light nuclei into a heavier one, as in stars
Transmutation
The conversion of one element into another through nuclear change
Radioisotope
An isotope with an unstable nucleus that undergoes decay
Carbon dating
Using carbon-14 decay to estimate the age of organic material
